{{Short description|Hungarian politician and scientist (1941–2013)}}
'''Árpád Duka-Zólyomi''' (8 May 1941 – 26 July 2013) was a [[Hungarians|Hungarian]] [[nuclear physicist]], university teacher and [[politician]] from [[Slovakia]]. He was deputy of [[National Council (Slovakia)|National Council]] from 1992 to 2004 and [[Member of the European Parliament]] with the [[Party of the Hungarian Coalition]], part of the [[European People's Party]], from 2004 to 2009.<ref name=ep>{{cite web|url=http://www.europarl.europa.eu/meps/en/28197/ARPAD_DUKA-ZOLYOMI_home.html |title=Arpad DUKA-ZÓLYOMI |publisher=European Parliament |date= |accessdate=2014-01-19}}</ref>

Duka-Zólyomi was born in [[Bratislava]]. He studied [[Gymnasium (school)|gymnasium]] in [[Galanta]] and then from 1958 to 1960 worked as laborer. From 1962 to 1968, he studied [[nuclear reactor physics]] at the [[Czech Technical University in Prague]],<ref name=cv>[http://www.dukazolyomi.sk/sk/index.php/zivotopis/ Árpád Duka-Zólyomi: Životopis] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202152047/http://www.dukazolyomi.sk/sk/index.php/zivotopis/ |date=2014-02-02 }}</ref> then worked as researcher and teacher at Faculty of Mathematics and Physics of [[Comenius University in Bratislava]]. From 1976 to 1989 he was researcher at Laboratory of Neutron Physics of [[Joint Institute for Nuclear Research]] ([[Dubna]], [[Russia]]), after he returned to Comenius University in Bratislava,<ref name=cv/> where he worked until 2008.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080913014151/http://www.dnp.fmph.uniba.sk/people.php Section of Nuclear Physics: Members of the Nuclear Physic Section]</ref>

From 1968 to 1970, he was chairman of Association of Hungarian Youth in Slovakia. He was a member of the political party [[Coexistence (political party)|Coexistence]] (1991–1998 vicechairman), then in 1998, the party merged into Party of the Hungarian Coalition, when he was from 1998 to 2005 vicechairman.

In [[1992 Slovak parliamentary election|1992 elections]] he was elected as member of National Council and reelected again in [[1994 Slovak parliamentary election|1994]], [[1994 Slovak parliamentary election|1998]] and [[2002 Slovak parliamentary election|2002]]. In [[2004 European Parliament election in Slovakia|2004 elections]] he was elected as member of European Parliament for Slovakia. In EP he was  substitute for the [[Committee on Foreign Affairs (EU)|Committee on Foreign Affairs]] and a vice-chair of the Delegation to the [[European Union|EU]]-Armenia, EU-Azerbaijan and EU-Georgia Parliamentary Cooperation Committees and a substitute for the Delegation for relations with Belarus. He was also chairman of the Slovak-Hungarian group of the [[Inter-Parliamentary Union]] (1998–2004), member of the EU-Slovak Republic Joint Parliamentary Committee (1995–2002), member of the [[Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe]] Parliamentary Assembly (2002–2004) and member of the [[Council of Europe]] Parliamentary Assembly (1999–2004).<ref name=cv/><ref name=ep/>

He died on 26 July 2013.<ref>[http://www.eppgroup.eu/press-release/Slovakia%3A-condolences-for-Árpád-Duka-Zólyomi http://www.eppgroup.eu/press-release/Slovakia%3A-condolences-for-Árpád-Duka-Zólyomi  Slovakia  condolences for Árpád Duka Zólyomi]</ref>
